name: veterinary_clinic_system_011_boarding_checkin_flow
instruction: Process the morning boarding arrivals. A reservation is ready for check-in if its status is 'reserved', its check_in date is on or before the episode date, and its assigned run is currently available (status 'available' or already occupied by the same patient from a previous run of this task). Process those reservations in ascending check_in order, breaking ties by reservation id. For each successfully checked-in guest: set the reservation status to 'checked_in'; set the run to 'occupied' with current_patient_id set to the reservation's patient; and send the owner an outbound email with subject 'Boarding check-in confirmed — {batch_code}' and body '{PetName} checked into {run_type} run {run_number} at {location_name} on {check_in_date}.' using the live owner_id, patient_id, run number, run type, and location name. If a run is not available, skip that reservation (it stays reserved for now). Finally, push one ops_reports row with report='boarding_checkin_manifest' and the live batch_code, containing the episode date, checked_in_count, skipped_count, by_location (count per location), and by_run_type (count per run type). If the manifest row already exists, overwrite it. The flow is idempotent.

success_criteria.summary: From live data: candidate reservations are reserved with check_in <= episode, sorted by (check_in, id). A reservation is processed only if its assigned run is available or already occupied by the same patient. Each processed reservation becomes 'checked_in'; its run becomes 'occupied' with matching current_patient_id; one outbound email per processed patient with the exact body keyed by patient_id. One ops_reports row (report='boarding_checkin_manifest', batch_code) holds the counts and by_location/by_run_type breakdowns, all verified via dual raw-row and SQL paths. All collections outside the blast radius are byte-identical to the seed snapshot.

checks.expect: Each processed candidate reservation is checked_in; all other reservations unchanged
Each processed candidate's run is occupied with correct current_patient_id; all other runs unchanged
One outbound email per processed patient with subject containing batch_code and body containing run_type, run_number, location_name, and check_in
Exactly one manifest row with correct counts, by_location, and by_run_type
Every aggregate count and breakdown agrees between a raw-row Python filter and an independent SQL GROUP BY/COUNT query

hazards: Run-availability decoys: among the reserved reservations with check_in <= 2026-09-30, several (reservation 98 for run 4, reservation 99 for run 3, and two pairs sharing a run — 85/17 on run 10, 65/6 on run 6) are assigned to runs that are already occupied or become occupied by an earlier guest. A solution that checks in the earliest reservation by date only, without verifying the run is free, will overbook and fail.

Episode-date sensitivity: at jitter -3 (ep 2026-09-27) only 8 reservations are candidates and only 5 can be checked in; at the base and jitter +3 dates 10 reservations are candidates and 6 can be checked in. The candidate set and the processed set both depend on the live episode date.

Tie-breaking and run conflicts: reservations 85 and 17 both point to cattery run 10, and 65 and 6 both point to kennel run 6. The correct first-come-first-served order (by check_in then id) checks in 85, skips 17, checks in 65, skips 6.

Communication and manifest deduplication: a second run must not send duplicate emails, must not duplicate the ops_reports row, and must leave the same set of reservations checked_in. Matching on subject and patient_id closes the duplicate-communication hole.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Fuses a single-reservation check-in into a multi-reservation arrival manifest: it respects run availability, skips overbooked or occupied-run reservations, sends per-guest owner communications, and produces a reconciled ops_reports manifest. The run-conflict and episode-date-sensitivity hazards require the agent to derive the target set from live data rather than a fixed id.
